relations.subject: Eido Tai Shimano
relations.evidence: In his youth Shimano was ordained as a novice monk by Kengan Goto, the priest of Empuku-ji, the Rinzai temple in Chichibu.

relations.subject: Eido Tai Shimano
relations.evidence: Later he was trained by Shirozou Keizan Roshi, abbot of Heirin-ji, near Tokyo.

relations.subject: Eido Tai Shimano
relations.evidence: In 1954, Shimano left to study at Ryutaku-ji and practice with Soen Nakagawa Roshi, a relatively young Zen teacher.

relations.subject: Eido Tai Shimano
relations.evidence: In 1954, Shimano left to study at Ryutaku-ji and practice with Soen Nakagawa Roshi... Shimano received Dharma transmission from Soen Nakagawa in 1972

relations.subject: Eido Tai Shimano
relations.evidence: His friend Bernard Phillips, an American Zen scholar, was returning home on the same ship, after doing research in Japan sponsored by the Zen Studies Society.

relations.subject: Eido Tai Shimano
relations.evidence: A few years later he became abbot of the Zen Studies Society... he would retire as abbot of the Zen Studies Society in December. He did so on December 8, 2010.

relations.subject: Shinge Roko Sherry Chayat
relations.evidence: Shinge Roko Sherry Chayat Roshi, who received dharma transmission in 1998, was installed as the new Abbot on January 1, 2011.

relations.subject: Shinge Roko Sherry Chayat
relations.evidence: Shimano encouraged everyone to accept his successor, Shinge Sherry Chayat, as their teacher... Dharma heirs... Sherry Chayat
